title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: The No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act would bar the construction of artificial‑intelligence data centers on land owned by the U.S. federal government. It aims to protect public resources, reduce energy consumption, and address security and privacy concerns by keeping AI infrastructure off federal property.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act seeks to shield households from the rising electricity expenses caused by large AI data centers. The bill aims to implement measures that regulate or curb the energy use of these facilities, ensuring that families are not burdened by high utility bills.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This act seeks to stop AI companies from charging excessively high prices and from fixing wages in ways that hurt consumers and workers. It proposes enforcement rules and penalties to ensure fair pricing and labor practices in the AI industry.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary halt on building and operating new data centers dedicated to AI, aiming to curb the sector’s rising energy consumption and environmental impact. It also requires comprehensive environmental assessments, stakeholder consultations, and a review period before any future AI data center projects can proceed.

title: To better coordinate Federal efforts to utilize advance technologies, such as artificial intelligence, to improve diagnoses, treatments, cures, and prevention strategies for pediatric cancer, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: This policy aims to improve federal coordination in using artificial intelligence to enhance the diagnosis, treatment, cure, and prevention of pediatric cancer. It also explores other potential uses of AI for medical research and patient care.

title: To provide for certain artificial intelligence agent discovery and security standards, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This policy establishes standards for discovering artificial intelligence agents and ensuring their security. It also addresses related regulatory and compliance matters.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Forwarded by Subcommittee to Full Committee by Voice Vote.
summary: The Open‑Source AI Leadership Act is designed to position the United States as a global AI innovation hub by promoting the development, sharing, and adoption of open‑source AI models and tools. It allocates government funding and tax incentives to research institutions and companies, establishes clear guidelines for transparency and responsible use, and encourages collaboration between the public and private sectors to accelerate open‑source AI progress.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 aims to establish a formal framework for studying how artificial intelligence tools are used in legal settings. It creates oversight mechanisms to ensure AI applications in courts are transparent, reliable, and protect fairness and due process.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Act creates a framework for studying how artificial intelligence is used in courts and for monitoring that use. It establishes a committee that reviews AI tools, sets guidelines, and tracks their impact on court operations.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that every American and community impacted by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should have the right to transparency and local autonomy.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives believes that anyone and every community affected by building or running an AI data center has a right to know what’s happening and to have a say in how it’s managed locally. This policy calls for full transparency and local autonomy for all affected Americans and communities.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 is a U.S. law that seeks to protect AI models from unauthorized copying and distribution. It establishes penalties and safeguards to make it easier for creators to enforce their rights and deter model theft.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 would require companies that use automated decision‑making tools to evaluate their algorithms for potential bias and impact on protected groups. It would also mandate public reporting and corrective actions if harmful outcomes are found.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is a proposed law that seeks to prevent artificial intelligence from being used to spread false or misleading information during elections. It would establish rules and safeguards—such as requiring clear labeling of AI‑generated content and limiting its use in political campaigns—to keep voters better informed and election processes more trustworthy.

title: Homestake AI Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.
summary: The Homestake AI Act of 2026 establishes a regulatory framework for the development and use of artificial intelligence within the state, focusing on transparency, accountability, and safety. It requires AI developers and users to meet strict data privacy standards, obtain licensing, and comply with oversight rules designed to protect consumers and ensure responsible AI deployment.

title: A concurrent resolution expressing the sense of Congress that the Ratepayer Protection Pledge announced on March 4, 2026, reflects sound national policy to protect ratepayers in the United States, promote electricity affordability, and ensure that all people of the United States, including households, small businesses, schools, hospitals, and farms, have access to reliable and affordable energy as artificial intelligence and data center infrastructure expands across the United States.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources. (text: CR S1618-1619)
summary: Congress has passed a resolution affirming that the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, announced in March 2026, is a sound national policy to safeguard ratepayers by ensuring electricity remains affordable and reliable. It emphasizes that all Americans—including households, businesses, schools, hospitals, and farms—should have access to dependable energy as AI and data‑center growth expands across the country.

title: Liquid Cooling for AI Act of 2025
action: Committee on Energy and Natural Resources Subcommittee on Energy. Hearings held. With printed Hearing: S.Hrg. 119-366.
summary: The Liquid Cooling for AI Act of 2025 sets out guidelines and incentives to encourage the use of liquid cooling technology in AI data centers, aiming to boost energy efficiency and reduce heat‑related downtime. It establishes performance standards, promotes research, and offers tax credits or other benefits to companies that implement certified liquid cooling systems.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 requires AI developers and users to evaluate and reduce the environmental footprint of their systems, such as the carbon emissions from training and running large models. It mandates reporting, accountability, and the use of carbon‑offset programs to encourage greener AI development and deployment.

title: PROACTIV Artificial Intelligence Data Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The PROACTIV Artificial Intelligence Data Act of 2025 is a proposed law that seeks to regulate how personal data is collected, stored, and used by artificial intelligence systems. It aims to protect individuals’ privacy by establishing standards for transparency, consent, and accountability in AI data practices.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 requires companies that use automated decision tools to evaluate the impact of their algorithms and identify any bias, discrimination, or privacy risks. It also mandates regular reporting, transparency about how these systems work, and measures to correct unfair outcomes.

title: Youth AI Privacy Act
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Youth AI Privacy Act is designed to safeguard the personal data of minors interacting with AI technologies. It establishes stricter rules for data collection, processing, and sharing to ensure children’s privacy and safety in digital environments.

title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026 creates rules that all AI‑powered toys sold to children must meet safety and privacy standards before they can be marketed. It requires manufacturers to test, certify, and report on their AI toy products to ensure they are secure, non‑harmful, and appropriate for young users.

title: Expanding AI Voices Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Expanding AI Voices Act proposes to broaden the range of AI technologies and applications that are permissible and encouraged. It aims to increase diversity in AI development, support new voices, and promote innovation across different sectors.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 is designed to establish a national framework for overseeing the creation, deployment, and operation of AI‑driven physical systems such as autonomous vehicles, drones, and robots. It aims to promote safety, interoperability, and collaboration among industry, regulators, and the public to ensure these systems are integrated responsibly and securely into everyday life.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary halt on building new AI data centers to address concerns about energy use, environmental impact, and societal implications. It encourages the adoption of more sustainable data infrastructure practices and calls for a thorough review of AI infrastructure’s long-term effects before any future construction.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Ready Data Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence-Ready Data Act is a proposed law that would set rules for how data is prepared, cleaned, and labeled so that it can be easily used by AI systems. It aims to create common standards and guidelines for data quality, privacy, and ethical use to help developers build better, more trustworthy AI.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 sets up a national framework for assessing the safety and potential harms of AI systems, aiming to protect public well‑being and privacy. It requires developers and companies to evaluate, document, and mitigate risks before deploying AI technology.

title: Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2026
action: Star Print ordered on the bill.
summary: The Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2026 is a proposed law that seeks to foster AI development by providing funding, research grants, and incentives for companies while setting up guidelines for responsible use. It aims to balance innovation with public safety by establishing oversight mechanisms, encouraging collaboration between industry and regulators, and ensuring that AI benefits society while minimizing risks.

title: VET Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The VET Artificial Intelligence Act sets out regulations for the design, deployment, and use of AI systems in VET, focusing on safety, transparency, and accountability. It requires risk assessments for high‑impact applications, mandates public disclosure of AI decision‑making processes, and establishes oversight bodies to enforce compliance and protect users.

title: NSF AI Education Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The NSF AI Education Act of 2026 aims to strengthen AI education nationwide by increasing federal funding for schools, colleges, and research institutions. It focuses on expanding interdisciplinary curricula, enhancing teacher training, and building a skilled workforce ready for the growing AI-driven economy.

title: CREATE AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The CREATE AI Act is a proposed European Union law that seeks to regulate the design, use, and deployment of artificial intelligence systems. It establishes principles, risk categories, and obligations to ensure AI technologies are safe, transparent, and respect fundamental rights.

title: Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2026 is a law that seeks to help small businesses learn how to build and use AI tools. It offers training programs, grants, and guidance so entrepreneurs can adopt AI responsibly and grow their businesses.

title: Small Business Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Small Business Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act is designed to help small businesses adopt AI by offering funding, training, and access to AI tools. It aims to lower barriers, boost competitiveness, and encourage innovation in the small‑business sector.

title: LIFT AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The LIFT AI Act is a proposed law aimed at improving the oversight and governance of artificial intelligence. It sets out new standards for transparency, safety, and accountability in AI development to protect users and promote ethical use.

title: Artificial Intelligence Scam Prevention Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Scam Prevention Act is designed to stop fraud that uses AI, requiring businesses to be clear about when and how AI is used and to provide safeguards against deceptive content. It also sets out penalties and oversight to protect consumers from AI‑generated scams.

title: States' Right to Regulate AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The States' Right to Regulate AI Act is a proposed law that would let each U.S. state create and enforce its own rules for developing and using artificial intelligence. It aims to give states the flexibility to address local concerns about AI safety, privacy, and ethics while ensuring that federal oversight does not override those state‑specific regulations.

title: Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025 seeks to protect individuals from discrimination and bias generated by AI systems, ensuring fair treatment across all protected classes. It establishes standards for transparency, accountability, and oversight so that AI developers and users must demonstrate compliance with civil rights principles in their design, deployment, and decision‑making processes.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2025 aims to strengthen the nation’s AI and critical technology talent pipeline by promoting targeted training and education programs. It proposes collaboration between government, academia, and industry to ensure a skilled workforce that supports national security and economic competitiveness.
